result: Clinical-grade WGS in 31 affected people from 25 families found pathogenic or likely pathogenic rare variants in 8 of 25 probands (32%) and 12 of 31 affected (39%), in heterogeneous energy-metabolism, ion-homeostasis and synaptic pathways.
reason: Measures rare monogenic variants by WGS, not familial recurrence risk or heritability; fits the rare-variant WGS finding, small and uncontrolled.

result: In 145 people with post-COVID fatigue, those ill more than 200 days had more fatigue, higher TMS cortical excitability, slower reaction times and more peripheral muscle fatigue than those ill under 200 days.
reason: Within-long-COVID duration comparison using TMS and reaction time; no grip fMRI/EEG motor-network measure or control comparison as in the finding.

result: In 145 people with post-COVID fatigue, those ill more than 200 days had more peripheral muscle fatigue, higher cortical excitability and slower reaction times than those ill under 200 days.
reason: Peripheral muscle fatigue method unspecified (not repeated maximal handgrip) and compared only by illness duration, not against controls.

result: In 50 long COVID patients vs 45 referred controls, peak VO2, exertional heart rate and VO2 at anaerobic threshold were similar.
reason: Same measure (peak VO2 on CPET) with no group difference, so a null result rather than an extension; controls are clinic referrals.

result: RER-based indirect calorimetry showed 73% of long COVID patients vs 20% of controls relied predominantly on carbohydrate rather than fat at rest, and carbohydrate use was higher in those with severe fatigue and PEM.
reason: Same substrate-use measure showing reduced fat oxidation, adds resting data and a link to PEM severity.

result: In 40 CFS vs 40 matched controls, 16S sequencing showed lower alpha-diversity and fewer Firmicutes, Clostridiales and Ruminococcaceae, fecal acetate and butyrate were lower (q<0.05), and Faecalibacterium/Ruminococcaceae correlated with butyrate (r=0.52-0.56).
reason: Independent cohort showing reduced butyrate-producing taxa and lower fecal butyrate, same direction.

result: On quantitative autonomic testing, long COVID patients had greater heart-rate rise and blood-pressure drop on active stand and tilt than controls, with age- and sex-adjusted dysfunction resembling pure autonomic failure.
reason: Same objective cardiovascular autonomic tests in referred long COVID, abnormal in the same direction; abstract truncated so numbers missing.

result: In 100 CFS vs 100 controls, DTI showed reduced FA in the left cingulum parolfactory and frontal-parahippocampal tracts (middle-posterior segment), and FA of these tracts classified CFS with 85% accuracy.
reason: Independent white-matter diffusion study, but uses conventional DTI FA with a focal cingulum result rather than the advanced-model widespread pattern, so extends rather than replicates.

result: About one year after mild COVID, people with cognitive PASC had raised blood neuronal and astroglial damage-associated proteins vs other PASC and controls, reproduced in an independent validation cohort.
reason: Long COVID version of blood neuronal/glial injury markers, raised only in the cognitive subgroup; specific proteins not named in abstract.

result: Cognitive PASC showed enlarged choroid plexus, increased hippocampal susceptibility and cingulate/insular cortical thinning across exploration and validation cohorts, not seen in other PASC.
reason: Same MRI structural measures including enlarged choroid plexus, adds a cognitive-subgroup restriction.
